Pensions Capture: Onward march of prescribed assets

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is the ANC dropping huge hints that they are about to raid private pension funds

Unique Selling Point:
confrontational interview with Enoch Godongwanwa

Summary:
Summary

Has the ANC made up its mind that it will take your hard- earned Pension funds and use them to stave off an IMF bailout?
As business warns government of runaway debt and absolutely nothing has been done since the elections to mitigate against government spending an IMF bailout is being increasingly discussed as inevitable.

But Enoch Godongwana – the ANC head of economic transformation has other plans. Why go to the IMF when you can simply raid the pensions of your private citizens.

In May Carte Blanche sat down with Enoch Godongwana in a robust interview.
At the time he told us:

“the resolution carefully crafted says we want to investigate prescribed assets, that is what the resolution says. The reason that we have crafted it in that way is that we don’t want to implement without clear thinking, on which asset classes and the cost to our economy.”

Alexander Forbes suggested that we should sleep but with one eye open. Well now only a few months later as talk of an IMF Bailout intensifies it seems that was good advice – In a recent interview with the Sunday Times it seems Godongwana has changed his tune and says “

“Why would you go to the IMF and the World Bank and go and raise money when we have sufficient savings in the economy which you can borrow, probably far cheaper and probably with little exchange rate risk?”

But then he wiggles out of making a clear pronouncement with further double speak, saying Borrowing from domestic markets is not prescribed Assets.


Further information:
But in response outspoken CIO of Future Growth Andrew Canter said compelling pension funds to invest in national development was unnecessary as there was no shortage of pension money for that.

Prescription is dangerous and would be very disruptive to the way capital markets which are a national asset work,” he said. “ We are very hostile to prescription, we think it’s a terrible idea

He said: “Current regulations compel pension funds to invest 75% of their assets in the country. That means that 75% of the money of pension funds is in the country and ready to invest in SA. How hard is that?

In a sequel to our first story we highlight the contradictions coming from the ANC on this highly charged matter. We speak to LEON CAMPHER CEO of ASISA the Association for Savings and Investment SOUTH AFRICA. Campher’s organisation is mandated by its members who manage R6.2 trillion of the nation’s savings.
For Campher they are the custodians of our savings and would oppose the deployment of savings into entities that have been mired in State Capture. This is why they oppose Prescribed Assets

• The concept of “prescribed assets” would force the savings and investment industry to deploy the savings of ordinary South Africans into entities that have over the recent past been mired in State Capture and lack of delivery. As custodians of these savings we have to oppose this.
• Asset managers are not asset owners. The bulk of the assets that could be prescribed are owned by retirement fund members. It also needs to be noted that roughly half of these assets are held by the GEPF and are therefore owned by public servants. As the owners of these assets, ordinary South Africans elect and appoint trustees to make asset allocation decisions that are in their best interest. Prescription would jeopardise this fiduciary duty.
• Prescription of assets interferes with the capital allocation function of the capital markets, which should always be objective and driven by performance. Forcing the market to invest in low yielding and/or high risk projects could have two direct consequences:
o The incentive for these projects to compete would be removed as funding would no longer be incentivised by performance.
o Given that capital is a finite resource, deserving projects could be deprived of funding. These projects that would otherwise have driven growth and created sustainable employment would now not happen anymore.
• Prescription would have a negative impact on the country’s credit rating. If South Africa loses its investment grade rating, foreign investors, many of whom are pension funds, would be forced to withdraw their money from South Africa. This is something the country can ill afford.


The DA Shadow minister for finance Geordin Hill- Lewis says they are drawing a line in the sand and are convinced the ANC will prescribe assets. Whatever it takes they will oppose prescription.






Locations:
CAPE TOWN & JOHANNESBURG

Script:


LINK
Just before the elections, Carte Blanche sat down with Enoch Godongwana, the man who would ultimately decide if the government would dip into your hard- earned retirement savings to fund state owned companies. And this is what he had to say ……

Enoch
So, you are singling out, deliberately in my view a scarecrow, that the only way we can do prescribed assets is to send it to an SOE, that is not what we are talking about!
Devi
But you are not categorically saying to me that won’t happen?
Enoch Godongwana
I said it won’t happen!
Devi
Guaranteed?
Enoch Godongwana
Guaranteed. It won’t happen

DEVI
Do you blame people for not having trust right now? They don’t trust….

Enoch
I don’t expect people to trust in the environment in which Eskom has performed. But I don’t expect when you talk about prescribed assets, of necessity, you mean we put them in SAA that is not what we are talking about!

Devi
The point I am making is that I don’t trust…

ENOCH
You are not the one who is going to make the decision about prescribed assets

Devi
No I am not, that is for sure!

Enoch
Then you should be listening to me I am the one who is going to make that decision about
prescribed assets

LINK
Three months later, and the mood in the country is heavy, and business is warning government about its runaway debt. Once again prescribed assets are on the agenda

Commentary One
South Africa has one of the biggest pension savings in the world in dollar terms, but as the state runs out of money, there is increasing concern that the ANC proposal to prescribe assets, will force your fund manager to invest in loss making assets. Andrew Canter, Chief investment officer of Future Growth

ANDREW CANTER
It’s a tax. It’s a money grab, it’s a tax, it’s an opportunity for politicians to channel money to their favourite causes

Commentary two
Pension funds are a national asset, and should not be instruments of state policy, he says

Andrew
if you talk about prescription it is roughly the same as saying, oh hey, there is a pot of money over there! I think I want to use it for that purpose. I have decided that, and I will make a regulation to say I will do it. Its roughly the same as saying there is a whole bunch of money in your bank account. I am going to take 5% of money in your bank account and make you put it somewhere. It’s a clear violation of property rights, so when we talk about prescription that is exactly what we are talking about, we are talking about a money grab.

Commentary Three
But in a recent Sunday Times interview, Godongwana says that borrowing from domestic markets is not the same as prescribed assets. Godongwana is quoted as saying the asset management industry which includes pension funds, should lend some of the billions its managing to the state.

But already pension funds do invest billions in bonds and state projects with good returns. But they do it willingly.

Andrew Canter
What we need is good projects to invest in, we need SOE to be run properly, and we will invest

Commentary four
But the debate on prescription continues. Leon Campher is the CEO of the Association for Savings and Investment SA. They oppose prescription

Leon
Our view is that there are enough sane people around in government and in private sector to understand that this shouldn’t happen.

Commentary Five
ASISA members manage R6.2 trillion of the nations savings

Leon
Currently there is about R2.9 trillion of foreign investment in our stock market and another trillion invested in the bond market. The minute you introduce prescription, there is a good chance all that money will leave, which could have quite a bad impact on our local markets, would probably depreciate our currency dramatically, and would be a flight of foreign capital which then would have an impact off your balance of payments, and then at some stage you probably would have to go to the IMF.

Commentary six
ASISA thinks prescribed assets may be a storm in a teacup, but when the DA asked President Ramaphosa for clarity in the National Assembly, it was not forthcoming.

Musi Maimane
In the context where investment is down, growth is down and unemployment at a record high will you tell the people of this country whether you do support the prescription of assets and the stealing of pension funds of South Africans?

President Ramaphosa
The more I listen to honourable Maimane the more he seems like a broken record

Commentary seven
The president appeared irritated by the question

Ramaphosa
The issue of prescribed assets has been discussed over and over again, and in the end Madame speaker we are going to pursue policies that are going to advance the interests of our people here in SA, and also advance the interests of pension fund holders

John Steenhuizen
Madame speaker, that is the type of answer you expect from a loan shark, not from a president question is clear do you support it or not

Commentary eight
The president would say no more, and our questions for clarity from Enoch Godongwana went unanswered. But the DA’s Geordin Hill- Lewis is of the view that it’s only a matter of time before prescription becomes government policy.

Geordin Hill- Lewis
It’s very difficult to get your pension out of South Africa because you can’t access your pension. Remember that unless you resign and take your pension out and pay an enormous amount in tax, your pension is basically locked in.

Andrew
You are already hearing of people saying how can I get my money out of my pension fund scheme, and where can I put it where it will be safe from people grabbing at it

Commentary nine (Fix pix)
And even if prescribed assets become a reality, they are unlikely to be much more than 3- 5% of your pension, but over a lifetime that can be substantial

Andrew
There have been stories of people who have actually quit their jobs so they can crystallize the value of their pension fund and take it away and then get re-employed somewhere else, that is how scared people are

Commentary ten
But Isaah Mhlanga, executive chief economist at Alexander Forbes still believes what he told us in May

Devi
Are you saying sleep easy all will be well?
Isaah
I say sleep, perhaps with one eye open, the moment it becomes government process then you need to open both eyes, but for now I think it’s a low probability event, but don’t completely discount because its being touted by the ruling party so it has some weight, it’s not a zero percent probability

Claire to Andrew
Give the guy who is sitting on the couch right now advice on what they can do to protect their money
In a sense its out of their hands so if push comes to shove, what we can all do is get on the streets with placards to protect our pension funds. It’s that serious.

Commentary eleven
Alternatively, he says we should look to the courts for relief. Canter has canvassed informal legal advice and studied our constitutional protections

Claire
So then what are our defences?
Andrew
Lets talk about the actual defences we have legally speaking. There is the famous property rights clause in the bill of rights. If the government for example says I am going to channel part of your pension fund into uneconomic investments, well I am taking away your property rights in two ways, aren’t I? Firstly, I am taking away your choice and I am reducing your returns which is another form of property I am taking from you.

Commentary twelve
Canter says we may also be able to use clause 27 that guarantees our rights to social security.

Andrew Canter
So here is the question I ask, can we use that clause to challenge prescription. It looks like yes. You are challenging my ability to provide my own social security and second does that mean the government takes on the obligations from my pension? So, if I don’t have enough money at retirement because you made me have lower returns, you pay! You made me do it, you made a law, you reduced my social security – the bill of rights say I have a right to social security – you pay me more pension!


THE END 08 01






PROMO ONE
The ANC manifesto wants to divert a portion of your retirement funds into the state’s preferred investment – will it become policy? …the president in parliament left more questions than answers…

PROMO TWO
Can you protect your pension if government decides to prescribe assets?
Andrew Canter
if push comes to shove the best we can all do is get on the streets with placards and protest to protect our pension funds.

PROMO THREE
Asset managers are concerned about the ANC’s investigations to use pension funds to pay for loss making State-Owned companies. How likely is it to happen and what can you do about it?

This is something the country can ill afford. The DA Shadow minister for finance Geordin Hill- Lewis says they are drawing a line in the sand and are convinced the ANC will prescribe assets. Whatever it takes they will oppose prescription.
